l.i: Admodum in turbidis Gracia Concionibus ve-
nalis orator. Scilicet illud est Deum suo ho-
nore & providentia communis & gratia
deturbare, homines etiam cum dispendio
salutis & solatii intumidare, nixos in vanum
prædicatis falso liberi arbitrij facultatibus
aut etiam Communi gratia quā fallax & inefficax,
multos, quibus contigit, in cœno destituit.
Hoc est pietatem & religionem in exilium a-
gere, dum homines docentur semet potius suas-
que opes respicere & conando agendoque eniti,
quàm supplicus[?] muliebribus, reflexisque in
Deum cordibus, ejus auxilium implorare.
Adeo universam Theologiam non turbant, sed
exturbant novi dogmatistæ, fabri ψευδῶν[?] δο-
ξῶν[?] vere παραδόξων[?], quas, ut tueantur[?], in
omnes se formas vertere, modo Scriptura dicta
planissima & evidentissimos S. S. sensus tor-
quendo eludere, modo philosophiam advocare,
ut qui propter habitum mentes suas in Scrip-
turis subegissent, nec offusis nebulis à tra-
mite recto in pravum abduci possent, acu-
mine spinarum rationis humanæ punctì[?] aut
sinuosis anfractibus exotica sapientia turbati de
via veritate dubitare inciperent. Ista artes
imperitis & inexercitatis successu haud pœni-
tendo imposuerunt. Solet autem sapiens be-

page.notes: Running head read as printed: "Præfatio ad Lectorem." Greek words in the second paragraph are uncertain and marked [?]: "ψευδῶν", "δοξῶν" and "παραδόξων" are my best reading of the printed letters. "tueantur" (printed as possibly "tneantur") and "supplicus" are doubtful. "punctì" is doubtful. The spelling "Gracia" is copied as printed. No page number or signature is visible. The catchword "ni-" is the first syllable of the next page.
